lead: Kentucky faces mountain flash floods, Ohio River flooding and severe storms. DryFlare helps owners from Louisville to eastern Kentucky get water out and dry out.
risk: flash floods in the mountains, river flooding and severe storms
why: In July 2022, days of heavy rain sent creeks in eastern Kentucky over their banks. Towns in Breathitt, Knott and Perry counties were destroyed, and dozens of people died. Steep hollows funnel water fast, and many homes sit right beside creeks. Floods hit the region again in 2025.

Western and central Kentucky face other threats. The December 2021 tornado tore through Mayfield and Bowling Green. The Ohio River floods Louisville and river towns in wet years. Around Bowling Green, limestone karst can send water into basements in odd places. Tennessee and West Virginia share many of these risks.
image_caption: Creeks in Kentucky's hollows can rise into homes in hours during heavy rain.
problems: Any home left wet for days
tips: Sign up for county flood alerts if you live near a creek.
Keep important papers in a waterproof box upstairs.
Mobile home owners should anchor homes and check skirting after storms.
After a flood, throw out food and drinks that touched floodwater.
insurance: Very few eastern Kentucky homes had flood insurance in 2022. Flood is a separate policy, and it takes 30 days to start.

faq.q: Is it safe to go back into my house after a Kentucky flood?
faq.a: Wait until officials say it is safe. Watch for gas leaks, damaged wiring and weak floors. Wear boots and gloves, because floodwater carries sewage and chemicals. Then call DryFlare to remove mud and water and start drying.

licensing: Kentucky has no statewide general contractor license. Some cities, such as Louisville, require local licensing. Plumbers, HVAC techs and electricians need state licenses.
